name: loft_is_not_a_cone
why: The criterion of the entry: «loft -- two circles of different diameter at two known heights, volume compared with the formula of the frustum of a cone, with a wider declared tolerance». The wider tolerance is really needed, and this case says by how much and why.
_why_the_number_does_not_come_out_exact: Circles D40 and D20 at a distance of 50. The formula of the frustum of a cone gives pi*50/3*(400+200+100) = 36651.91. The loft makes 36650.61: it is MISSING 1.30 mm3, that is 35 millionths. It is not measurement noise and it is always in the same direction: the surface of a loft between two circles is a SPLINE APPROXIMATION of the conic, not a conic. Whoever compares a loft with the formula and does not know this chases a defect that is not there.
_why_the_cone_is_made_first: Because the way to show that the deviation comes from the LOFT and not from the formula is to build the same shape in another way, and `revolve` on the trapezoid (0,0)-(0,20)-(50,10)-(50,0) makes the same frustum of a cone exactly. It goes first because `revolve` has a guardian of its own that refuses if the document ends up with more than one body -- and it is right to have one: a profile that splits in two is almost always a wrong profile. The loft, which comes after, simply declares the two bodies.
_why_the_cone_is_at_two_hundred_millimet: The trapezoid is translated by 200 mm along the axis of the sketch so that the two solids do not touch: if they intersected, the total volume would no longer be the sum of the two, and the comparison would say nothing. The shape is the same, moved.

expect.tolerance_why: it is pi*50/3*700: the calculation has pi inside, and a revolution of a trapezoid is an EXACT frustum of a cone -- five hundredths are more than enough
expect.why: THE BENCHMARK, AND IT COMES OUT EXACT. This is the number of the formula, built by SOLIDWORKS another way. It serves to say that in the next step it is the LOFT that deviates, not the formula that is wrong.

expect.tolerance_why: it is the same formula as the step above, computed by the operation
the volume of a spline surface depends on the tessellation: half a cubic millimetre out of thirty-six thousand is noise, and stays narrower than the 1.30 that separates the loft from the cone
expect.why: THE LOFT WEIGHS LESS THAN THE CONE in the same part, and the difference is 1.30 mm3. The two solids have the same declared shape and two different volumes: that is the fact.

expect.tolerance_why: the relative deviation is 3.55 hundred-thousandths: the tolerance keeps it distinct both from zero and from a real error
expect.why: THE NUMBER THAT SAYS IT IS NOT A CONE. It is not zero -- and it must not be: if one day it became zero it would mean that SOLIDWORKS changed the way it builds lofts, and that is something to know. If it became large, it would mean the loft took another path.
the plane of the second circle: the operation makes it by itself, and declares it instead of letting it appear in the tree without explanation

expect.tolerance_why: it is the exact cone (36651.91) plus the loft (36650.61): one cubic millimetre covers the noise of both
expect.why: THE SUM IS THE PROOF. 36651.91 + 36650.61 = 73302.53. If the formula were wrong the two bodies would weigh the same and the sum would be 73301.23 or 73303.83. It is the difference between «my numbers do not add up» and «I know which of the two is approximated».
